Here is your AI digest for Wednesday, November 18, 2026.

---

**🔥 THE BIG STORY**

The AI world is reeling from the chaos at Nvidia, the company that builds the very foundation of the industry. Following the ouster of founder and CEO Jensen Huang last week, the chip giant is now under SEC investigation, has confirmed it will not reappoint him, and announced a full withdrawal from the Chinese market. The interim leadership is scrambling to calm nerves with pay raises and equity bumps for employees, but the damage is done. This isn't just a corporate drama; it's a geopolitical earthquake that injects massive instability into the global AI supply chain, proving that the future of AI will be shaped as much by scandals and statecraft as by silicon.

---

**🛠️ TOOL DROPS & UPDATES**

*   **Gemini gets more accessible and private.**
    The Gemini mobile app now runs on lower-memory Android devices, bringing multimodal features to a much wider audience. Google also expanded access to Gemini Tasks, which can handle calls and purchases, and rolled out "temporary threads" in its Search AI Mode, an incognito feature that prevents chats from being saved to your history. [S14][S149][S2]

*   **OpenAI details its new Codex sandbox.**
    A new blog post explains how Codex can now safely execute code and system commands on a user's machine, enforcing developer-controlled filesystem and network limits across major operating systems. This is a critical step for building more capable and trustworthy AI agents. [S77]

*   **ChatGPT to feature journalism from Le Figaro.**
    OpenAI has partnered with the French media outlet Le Groupe Figaro. ChatGPT will now be able to provide summaries and excerpts from the newspaper's articles, with clear attribution and links back to the original source. [S110]

---

**🎯 USE CASE SPOTLIGHT — BY ROLE**

*   **📣 Product Marketer**
    Use Google Search's new "temporary threads" feature to conduct competitor and keyword research without your own search history biasing the results. This gives you a cleaner, more objective view of how your brand and rivals appear to a neutral user. [S2]

*   **📋 Product Manager**
    Start auditing your team's internal documentation (PRDs, user research, meeting notes) in preparation for tools like Unsiloed AI, which just got funded. The goal is to structure your knowledge base so an internal AI agent can query it, drastically speeding up new hire onboarding and cross-team discovery. [S56]

*   **🎨 Designer (UI/UX)**
    Prototype a "vibe-based" onboarding flow for your next app, inspired by the "vibe-coding" trend. Instead of asking users about features, ask them about aesthetics, feelings, or desired outcomes to create a more emotionally resonant and personalized initial experience. [S67]

*   **📸 Photographer**
    Today's data offered no new specific tools or use cases for photographers.

*   **🎬 Videographer & Filmmaker**
    Today's data offered no new specific tools or use cases for videographers.

*   **📱 App Developer**
    Leverage the new OpenAI Codex sandbox to build features where an AI agent can safely execute commands on a user's machine. You can now build more powerful, agentic apps that interact with the local environment while respecting user-defined permissions for files and network access. [S77]

---

**🔬 FROM THE LABS**

**OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra is now designing chips.**
In a major leap for AI in the physical sciences, OpenAI has revealed it's using its models to assist in semiconductor design. An internal model, named GPT-6 Astra, successfully optimized circuits for a piece of silicon and improved designs for RISC-V cores. This beats previous methods by automating parts of a highly complex, human-driven process. In the next 6-12 months, this could dramatically shorten chip design cycles, allowing for more specialized, efficient, and cheaper AI hardware to come to market faster. [S109]

---

**🚚 AI IN LOGISTICS & SUPPLY CHAIN**

*   **DHL deploys AI for smarter international shipping.**
    DHL Express in the U.S. has rolled out an AI-powered system for item identification. The tool helps automate the complex and error-prone process of classifying goods for international customs, aiming to speed up transit times and improve compliance. [S17]

*   **Warehouse automation gets two big M&A deals.**
    Industrial giant Rockwell Automation is on a shopping spree, acquiring autonomous mobile robot (AMR) developer AGILOX and another robotic materials handling company. This signals aggressive consolidation in the warehouse robotics space as major players build out end-to-end automation portfolios. [S7][S22]

*   **Pedestal AI launches with $4.7M to build supply chain agents.**
    A new startup, Pedestal AI, has raised a seed round to build AI agents specifically for enterprise logistics. This move reflects a broader trend of venture money flowing into vertical-specific agents that can automate complex operational workflows. [S38][S60]

*   **UPS doubles down on healthcare logistics with acquisition.**
    UPS is acquiring Smartway Logistics, an Australian specialist in healthcare logistics. This strategic purchase underscores the growing importance of high-value, temperature-controlled supply chains and UPS's push to dominate the niche. [S122]

*   **Amazon's drone program faces local pushback amid national expansion.**
    While Amazon drone deliveries are launching or being approved in Ohio and Iowa, a Massachusetts town is revolting against the service, citing noise and privacy concerns. This highlights the growing friction between the tech giants' logistics ambitions and community acceptance on the ground. [S6][S92][S105]

*   **AI's role in warehousing is set to explode.**
    A new study predicts that by 2028, AI will be making a quarter of all warehouse decisions autonomously for half of all companies. This follows another report that 90% of supply chain organizations plan to increase their AI investments. [S9][S73][S86]

---

**💸 MONEY & MOVES**

*   **Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking.**
    The massive round signals Wall Street's hunger to use AI agents to eliminate the tedious grunt work of updating financial models and presentations, freeing up bankers for higher-value tasks. [S146]

*   **Humyn Labs lands $47M to feed data to robotics firms.**
    The India-based startup will supply specialized training data to U.S. robotics companies, signaling that high-quality, human-annotated data for physical AI remains a massive and lucrative market. [S61]

*   **Uniloed AI gets $7.5M to read enterprise documents.**
    Felicis led the seed round to help AI agents understand the messy, unstructured data locked in enterprise documents, a critical bottleneck for widespread AI adoption in the corporate world. [S56]

*   **Pedestal AI raises $4.7M for supply chain agents.**
    Led by Eclipse, the funding will help the startup build AI agents to automate complex logistics operations, showing investor confidence in vertical-specific AI automation. [S38][S60]

---

**🤖 OPEN SOURCE WATCH**

Today's data did not contain any specific new or fast-rising open-source repositories.

---

**🗣️ HACKER NEWS PULSE**

Today's data did not contain any posts from Hacker News.

---

**⚡ SPEED ROUND**

*   Nvidia’s board has no plans to bring back ousted CEO Jensen Huang, despite pressure from high-profile supporters. [S132]
*   Google Search’s new AI Mode now has an "incognito" option called temporary threads that doesn't save your chat history. [S2]
*   Banks like Citi are warning customers they are on their own if their finances are hacked while using third-party AI agents. [S11]
*   A new point-and-shoot AI hacking tool called "Artex" is making it easier for novice criminals to launch cyberattacks. [S24]
*   A Gallup report finds that Gen Z-ers who rely on AI for friendship report higher rates of loneliness. [S88]
*   AI startup Osmo claims its AI-powered "digital nose" is now as good as a human's at identifying and classifying smells. [S65]
*   Sam Altman is publicly warning against a future where AI, not humans, is in control of major decisions. [S16]
*   In a bizarre sign of the times, Google proactively announced that Gmail was *not* having an outage. [S137]
*   Disney and AWS are partnering to create AI-powered ‘Star Wars’ robots. [S70]

---

**🎮 TODAY'S DAILY CHALLENGE — TRY THIS IN 15 MINUTES**

Test drive the new privacy-focused AI conversations in Google Search.

*   **Tool to use:** Google Search (on any browser or the Google app).
*   **The exact workflow to try:**
    1.  Go to google.com and make sure you are in the AI-native search experience.
    2.  Find the option to start a "temporary thread" (this is Google's new incognito mode for AI chats).
    3.  Use the prompt: `"I'm planning a surprise weekend trip for my partner's birthday. Their ideal vibe is cozy, quiet, and somewhere with great hiking within a 3-hour drive of San Francisco. They dislike big crowds and tourist traps. Give me a few unique town/area suggestions, including a specific recommendation for a hotel or cabin in each."`
    4.  After the conversation, check your Google activity/search history. The chat should not be there.
*   **What I'm testing for:** Experience what an ephemeral, private AI conversation feels like. Does it change the kinds of questions you're willing to ask? Can you confirm it's not saved to your account history?
*   **Why this matters right now:** This is one of the first implementations of private AI chats in a major, mainstream product. It directly addresses user fears about AI logging every thought and query, setting a new standard for user privacy in the agentic era. [S2]

---

**🧠 EDGE INSIGHT**

The era of "move fast and break things" for AI agents is dying before it truly began. Today's news reveals a powerful counter-current to the hype around agent capabilities: a rapid pivot to containment and liability. Banks are already disavowing responsibility for customers using financial agents [S11], OpenAI is shipping sandboxes to limit what agents can do [S77], and security researchers are sounding the alarm on agent-driven attacks [S25].

The smartest builders aren't just asking "What can my agent do?" anymore. They're asking "What am I liable for if it does it?" The next 90 days will see an explosion of what can be called "AI governance tech"—permissioning frameworks, specialized insurance, and auditable logging—as the industry wakes up to the fact that you can't ship an autonomous actor into the world without guardrails and an answer for when things go wrong. The race for capability is now secondary to the race for control.
